$meta.name: Claude of Tanks design tokens
$meta.author: Kevin B. Liu
$meta.spec: brand-ui SPEC §4.2-4.14 (Direction B 'Premiere'); owner type ruling 2026-10-17 for the families
$meta.generator: tools/gen-tokens.mjs writes src/ui/tokens/tokens.css and src/ui/tokens/tokens.ts; tokens.selftest.mjs proves they match
$meta.rules: Colours are OKLCH sources emitted as hex. Components read semantic or component tokens, never primitives. Keys are CSS custom-property names without '--'.

tungsten.$description: The one brand amber; tungsten-500 replaces the ~58 near-duplicate ambers in use

family.$description: Owner ruling 2026-10-17: Chakra Petch (display 500/600/700), IBM Plex Sans (body 400/500/600), IBM Plex Mono (data 400/500), all SIL OFL, self-hosted by the type package. CJK uses system faces after the Latin face.

font-display.value: 'Chakra Petch','Cot Symbols','Cot Display Fallback','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC',sans-serif
font-display.$use: Display moments: Chakra Petch, then the marks face and the metric-matched local fallback (src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.display, which tokens.selftest.mjs holds equal), then the CJK system faces

font-body.value: 'IBM Plex Sans','Cot Accents','Cot Symbols','Cot Body Fallback','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC',sans-serif
font-body.$use: Reading text: IBM Plex Sans, the accents and marks faces, the metric-matched fallback, then the CJK system faces (equal to src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.body)

font-mono.$use: Live readouts (tabular figures through .num only): IBM Plex Mono, then its metric-matched fallback (equal to src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.mono)

family.font-cjk: 'IBM Plex Sans','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC','Source Han Sans SC',sans-serif

scale.$description: Runtime scale switches. --cot-ui-scale (0.78-1.08) is written by responsiveLayout.ts today. Nothing writes --cot-hud-fit (clamp(shortSide/1080,.85,2)) or the user factors (Text size 0.8-2.0, HUD size 0.75-1.5) yet: the accessibility core (BUI-F9) and the HUD restyle (BUI-H1) add those writers, so until then --cot-hud-scale is 1 and --cot-type-scale follows --cot-ui-scale alone.

font-size.$description: CSS px at 100 %. Nothing a player must read is below 11 px.

space.$description: 4 px base; retires the off-grid 5/7/9/13 px values

ease-exit.$use: At about 70 % of the enter duration

ease-move.$use: In-place travel (the shipped --cot-ease-move curve, kept so its consumers keep their feel)

font.$use: The reading face (SPEC 4.14 --font, owner ruling: IBM Plex Sans). Shell controls read --font-ui, display moments --font-display, live readouts --font-mono.

font-ui.value: 'Cot UI','Cot Accents','Cot Symbols','Cot Fallback','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC',sans-serif
font-ui.$use: The shell's weight-voiced family every surface renders ('Cot UI': Plex Sans 400/500, Chakra Petch 600/700), equal to FONT_STACK in src/ui/fonts.ts and to src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.ui (canvas text cannot read var(), so fonts.ts repeats the literal)

surface-plate.$use: Shell plates over stills and the live garage

ink-4.$never: Any text a player must read

line.$description: SPEC 4.3 gives line-1/2/3 (paper-50 at 7 / 13 / 24 %, pinned to the 4.14 sheet) to hairlines, control borders and strong rules, and SPEC 4.4 requires every control border a player must perceive to reach 3:1. line-2 measures 1.38-1.44:1, so the three lines stay decoration and the control border is its own token, --line-control, measured at 3:1 or more on every surface and plate

line-1.$never: The only boundary of a control (--line-control)

line-2.$use: Card and menu rings (e2, e3) and dividers (decoration)
line-2.$never: The only boundary of a control (--line-control)

line-3.$never: The only boundary of a control (--line-control)

line-control.$use: Control borders: secondary buttons, chips, inputs, toggles, checkboxes (SPEC 4.4: >= 3:1 on page, raised, menu, hover and both plates over bright imagery)

accent.$use: Primary action fill, selection edge, wordmark rule
accent.$never: Warnings, objectives, module identity, rewards, decoration

team-own.$use: Allies everywhere, drawn as a chevron

team-enemy.$use: Enemies everywhere, drawn as a diamond
team-enemy.$never: Danger state in the same element

team-squad.$use: Squad, the player's own marker accents, drawn as a dot

warn.$use: Damaged modules, caution; always with the 45° hatch

text-tone.$description: Coloured text: team names, state words, accent counts and text buttons. Each reads its colour role, and the high-contrast preset turns every one to ink-1 (SPEC 4.6: all text ink-1 or ink-2, 7:1), leaving the colour to the glyph beside the word. Text over imagery sits on a plate; vermilion text needs the .92 HUD plate

text-enemy.$never: Text on --surface-plate over bright imagery (4.23:1 over white): the .92 HUD plate

text-danger.$use: Destroyed or critical words, beside the cross
text-danger.$never: Text on --surface-plate over bright imagery (4.23:1 over white): the .92 HUD plate

text-accent.$use: Accent-coloured counts, text buttons and links (the one brand amber)

outcome.$description: Okabe-Ito based; analysis contexts only (Gallery protection, hit cam, shot report, kill cam, docs), never the HUD reticle. Ricochet is striped; spaced/no-damage is a dotted outline only.

protection.$description: Clipped cividis, thin = bright, absolute mm: <40, 80, 180, 350, 500, 650, 650+. Luminance falls monotonically so the ramp reads in greyscale.

system.$description: Anatomy identity, always with glyph + label; state is pattern + colour

role.$description: Crew roles: the letter glyph is mandatory (deutan ΔE between roles falls to ~9.5)

elevation.$description: Plates, not glass. backdrop-filter is never used over a live WebGL canvas.

inset.$description: Shell edges: max(24 px, 3 % of the short side) + the safe area; the HUD adds the crosshair safe zone

shape.$description: 0 for plates, 2 px for controls, 4 px for cards and sheets, pill only for chips; circles only for joysticks, blips and dials

button.$description: SPEC 6.1-6.2: one primary per view; heights 36 / 48 / 56 / 64 px; pressed = 1 px drop + accent-lo (primary) or the strong rule (others); disabled = ink-4, never hatch

target-min.$use: Minimum hit area of any control (icon buttons draw 36 px on dense desktop rails inside it)

btn-secondary-fill.$use: Secondary: 6 % paper fill with the control border

btn-press-edge.$use: Pressed secondary and danger buttons: the edge steps up from the control border to the label ink

btn-danger-edge.$use: Danger: vermilion outline + glyph; destructive actions take a confirm step

chip.$description: Chips, filter chips and tags (pill radius only here); selected = accent wash + accent edge

selected-edge.$use: Selected state: accent edge on the leading side or a full outline

type-effect.$description: Owner UI rule 5 (2026-10-17): display moments use the accent colour or the landing's hollow outline type, deliberately and at display sizes only (44 px and up). The landing's Latin headline is truly hollow (src/presentation/home.css .v5-hero-copy h1 span: color:transparent; -webkit-text-stroke:1.5px; text-shadow 0 8px 28px, pinned by tokens.selftest.mjs). The type package's .t-hollow reads --hollow-stroke and --hollow-ink. Never on CJK (SPEC 4.7): zh display type stays solid.

hollow-stroke.$use: -webkit-text-stroke width of hollow display type (the landing headline's 1.5 px)

hollow-fill.$use: Hollow type has no fill (the landing's color:transparent); never paint-order tricks, which cover the stroke's inner half

hollow-shadow.$use: text-shadow of hollow type: the landing headline's, which keeps the 1.5 px outline readable over bright media

hud-font.$use: HUD copy (battleHudLayout.css and hud.ts read var(--hud-font)): the shell family, as each document's type head declares it (typeFaces.ts typeTokenCss)

hud-type.$description: HUD floors at 1080p: 13 px copy, 14 px body, 20 px numerals

focus-bracket.$description: Registration brackets on cards, 3D picks, roster tiles and gamepad focus: focus is a shape, not only a colour

warn-hatch.$use: 45° damaged hatch spacing (deutan/protan presets double the density)

team-squad-ring.$use: Squad ring width (the tritan preset draws the ring)

preset.$description: SPEC 4.6. CSS: :root[data-<axis>=<preset>]; tokens.ts: TOKEN_PRESETS / tokenValue(). No surface hard-codes a team colour.

cvd.$tradeoff: Shape-coded pairs (team colours against each other, the objective neutral and the accent) keep a ΔE floor of 12 in every preset and the views it serves; two SPEC 4.6 presets fall below it and are pinned here, so any change to these colours reopens the decision. (1) Deuteranopia / protanopia: SPEC 4.6's orange enemy (#E69F00) shares the tungsten accent's hue, so enemy~accent falls to 10.0 normal, 7.3 deutan, 3.6 protan, in return for enemy~squad 33.2 -> 57.9 deutan and 28.4 -> 46.4 protan. Not the only option: keeping enemy vermilion and moving squad to paper-50 with the ring (the tritan treatment) keeps enemy~accent at 21.1 deutan / 41.5 protan and gives enemy~squad 52.8 / 50.1, but moves the weak pair to squad~neutral (4.1 / 4.2). tokens.selftest.mjs measures that alternative ($alternative) beside the shipped preset. The shipped preset is SPEC 4.6's; switching is a SPEC amendment to settle before the accessibility core (BUI-F9) gives players the setting. Until then nothing sets data-cvd. (2) Tritanopia: squad on paper-50 sits beside the objective neutral (paper-100) at 4.2 normal, 4.0 tritan. In both cases the shape carries the difference (enemy diamond against accent chrome, which is never diamond-shaped; squad dot with its 2 px ring against objective outlines), and the HUD restyle (BUI-H1) owns that shape coding.

high.$description: SPEC 4.6: HUD plates .96, all text ink-1 or ink-2 (7:1), line-3 borders. line-3 itself rises to 3:1 on every surface (SPEC 4.4's non-text floor), and the control border to 4.5:1 so controls stay a step above plate edges

alias.$description: Legacy names kept working during migration. Each lives in the file that already owns it as var(--<token>,<fallback>); the fallback equals the token's resolved value (pinned by tokens.selftest.mjs) so pages and fixtures without tokens.css render the same. $was is the value the name shipped with: each name aliases the nearest token of its target's family (colours by the CIE76 distance of the shipped colour over black and over white, durations by milliseconds, easings by the largest difference in progress), and the selftest proves that and prints every shift. SPEC 4.12 names the duration moves (instant 90 -> 80, base 190 -> 220, scene 420 -> 360); slow, drawer and soft follow the nearest-token rule. A $spec entry is a SPEC-named fold that overrides the nearest-token rule: SPEC 4.2 folds #ffd27a (x34) into tungsten-500, so --cot-gold, which colours text, reads the accent text role. The duration and easing moves change motion timing, which still frames cannot show: they are SPEC 4.12's intended changes, not part of the 'no visual change' parity.
